MANDATE_ANALYSIS.title: What membership means in YOUNGO
MANDATE_ANALYSIS.lede: YOUNGO is the Children and Youth Constituency of the UNFCCC. It groups youth NGOs admitted to the UNFCCC and engaged in international climate negotiations — and also welcomes non-NGO youth groupings and individual youth who face barriers to the formal observer system.

points.title: Who can join
points.body: Children and youth-led organisations, collectives, associations, movements, UNFCCC-admitted NGOs affiliated with the Youth Constituency that advance climate action and future generations’ rights — or any young person aged 34 and under.

points.title: Two membership tracks
points.body: YOUNGO Network is the open engagement layer (updates, actions, sharing, light support). Constituency Work is the deeper layer: internal coordination, WGs/OTs/task forces, policy and advocacy, Workspace access, decision-making, and eligibility for mandated roles — after formal onboarding.

points.title: Duties that come with membership
points.body: All engagement must follow YOUNGO Principles, Code of Conduct, Safeguarding, Child Safeguarding, and Conflict of Interest policies. You may only speak or act for YOUNGO if selected through a formal process. Conflicts of interest must be declared at registration.

points.title: How Constituency Work stays current
points.body: Onboarding runs every July and December. Constituency Work membership must be renewed every February (one-month window). Miss it and you drop back to the Network; you can rejoin via the normal process.

points.title: How membership ends
points.body: Resignation (email the Membership Team), expiration (individual membership ends at age 35; Constituency Work expires if not renewed), or termination for policy violations. On exit, YOUNGO data must be handed over within two weeks.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: Preamble
paragraphs: YOUNGO, as the Children and Youth Constituency of the UNFCCC, groups all youth NGOs admitted to the UNFCCC and engaged in international climate negotiations.

YOUNGO aims to give a voice to all children and youth worldwide who are concerned about climate change, and recognizes that many of them face significant barriers to engaging through the UNFCCC’s observer mechanism. Therefore, it also welcomes the membership of non-NGO youth groupings as well as individual youth who wish to engage and contribute in its efforts to achieve a livable planet for current and future generations.
The following Policy defines membership in YOUNGO.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §1 Registration
paragraphs: Every children and youth-led organisation, collective, association, movement, etc. or all UNFCCC admitted NGO which have indicated affiliation with the “Youth Constituency”, that work to promote ambitious climate action and protect the rights of future generations, or any young person who is 34 years old and under can register to become a YOUNGO member by filling out the membership registration form.

Organisations must name a Designated Contact Point (DCP), who must be an individual member and thus fulfill the individual membership requirements. In case an admitted NGO’s official Designated Contact Point to UNFCCC does not fulfill individual membership requirements, the NGO must assign a YOUNGO-specific Representative who meets the individual membership requirements.

Individuals and organisations must declare any potential conflicts of interest, according to the respective Policy, at the time of registration. Failure to do so can lead to non-admission or termination of membership.
In addition to the above requirements, individuals under 18 years old must also provide a signed Guardian Consent Form as part of their registration.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §1.1 Types of membership
paragraphs: Every member has the right to engage virtually and physically in YOUNGO’s events (including but not limited to YOUNGO’s daily coordination meeting at Conferences, side events, and L/R/GCOY). In all engagements members must adhere to YOUNGO’s policies and guidelines, including but not limited to its Principles, Code of Conduct, Safeguarding Policy, Child Safeguarding Policy, and Conflict of Interest Policy.
Individuals and organisations can choose to become either Members of the YOUNGO Network or Members of the Constituency Work.

bullets.label: Members of the YOUNGO Network
items: Receive regular update newsletters
Participate in YOUNGO actions, campaigns, events and opportunities
Share their own actions, campaigns, events and opportunities
Share information with and provide advice to the Constituency Work Members

Receive, upon request, support in navigating the UNFCCC admission process for NGOs (priority for NGOs led by marginalized children and youth and NGOs from developing countries as defined by the UNFCCC)

bullets.label: Members of the Constituency Work
items: All rights of YOUNGO Network members, plus:
Participate in the internal organisation and coordination work of YOUNGO and its teams
Participate in Working Groups, Operational Teams and ad-hoc Task Forces
Contribute to policy work and assist in providing strategic direction
Contribute to intervention texts, bilaterals and other advocacy work
Receive a YOUNGO Google Workspace account

Receive, upon request and depending on resources, translation and interpretation in all UN languages, as well as plain language and child-friendly versions for onboarding and crucial decision-making documents
Participate in decision-making according to the Governance Policy and YOUNGO Decision-Making Processes
Apply for mandated roles within the constituency (liaisons, contact points, focal points, etc.) according to applicable selection guidelines

paragraphsAfter: Members may only speak or act on behalf of YOUNGO, as a whole or in parts (e.g. Working Groups), if selected through a formal process according to YOUNGO’s guidelines.

People who register to join Constituency Work must complete an onboarding before being able to join and receive access to all benefits. Onboarding is conducted by the Membership Team every July and December to ensure new members have time to contribute meaningfully prior to major Conferences.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §1.2 Renewal
paragraphs: Members of the Constituency Work must renew their membership in Constituency Work every February. The Membership Team will request all Constituency Work members to reconfirm their membership within one (1) month of the request.

Failure to renew membership will lead to the expiration of membership in Constituency Work. Members will continue to be part of the YOUNGO Network and can rejoin the Constituency Work through the process outlined in §1.1.

For the purpose of counting the amount of years a member has been in Constituency Work, only their last joining date will be used. A grace period is given for members who do not reconfirm their membership in February, but rejoin the Constituency Work in July.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §1.3 Changes
paragraphs: If a member wishes to change any of their registration information, they can do so by emailing the membership team at membership@youngoclimate.org.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §2 End of membership
paragraphs: Membership can end through resignation, expiration, or termination.
In all cases members must hand over all YOUNGO data within 2 weeks of the notice of the end of their membership.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §2.1 Resignation
paragraphs: Members can voluntarily resign at any point by emailing the Membership Team at membership@youngoclimate.org.
The Membership Team will remove the member from all YOUNGO services within one (1) month of the receipt of the request.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §2.2 Expiration
paragraphs: Individual membership expires by the birthday on which the member turns 35 years old or in case of the death.
Membership of Constituency Work expires when a member fails to renew their membership as described in §1.2.
The Membership Team will remove members whose membership has expired from all YOUNGO services on a regular basis, at least once a month.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §2.3 Termination
paragraphs: Members who are found to have violated YOUNGO's policies may be subject to termination of their membership according to the Code of Conduct and other relevant policies.
The Membership Team will remove the member from all YOUNGO services immediately.

POLICY_SECTIONS.heading: §3 Implementation
paragraphs: The Membership Team is responsible for maintaining the registration form and the associated registry of members, conducting onboarding calls every July and December, as well as carrying out any other tasks associated with the implementation of this policy.

presentation: ACE WG works on Action for Climate Empowerment — education, training, public awareness, public participation, public access to information, and international cooperation on those elements.
The group tracks the Glasgow work programme on ACE, the ACE Dialogue, and related COP/SB inputs, including ACE Day and side-event coordination toward COP31.
2026 Contact Points Adigao Alvin Wenia (Alvin Adigao) and Felipe Gómez Gallo facilitate the join form and WhatsApp channel. Register with YOUNGO first, then complete the ACE form.
rules: Prioritise child- and youth-friendly communication.
Coordinate ACE Dialogue, ACE Day, and education-related inputs with the group before speaking for YOUNGO.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.

presentation: Arts, Culture and Heritage WG brings artists, storytellers, heritage practitioners, and advocates into YOUNGO’s climate work.

The group has contributed to youth inputs on how culture, heritage, storytelling, and creative industries show up in climate frameworks, including a 2026 cross-WG consultation on the Culture Global Stocktake.
2026 Contact Points Samuel Rubin and Anirudh Janagam facilitate the member WhatsApp. Complete this onboarding to open the channel — the invite is not public.
rules: Credit collective and community cultural work; do not extract or publish others’ cultural material without consent.
Coordinate public statements and CGST or COP culture inputs with CPs before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.

presentation: The Adaptation Working Group builds youth negotiation and technical capacity on UNFCCC adaptation tracks, especially the Global Goal on Adaptation (including the UAE–Belém work programme and follow-up) and National Adaptation Plans.
2026 Contact Points are Gaël Bizet and Levina Oyugah. Membership is for YOUNGO members aged 35 and under; complete the public join form, then watch CP channels for calls.
At SB64 the WG worked with UNICEF, UNFPA, Save the Children, and Young Lives on a child- and youth-responsive GGA brief, and kept a central working document and session WhatsApp for coordination.
rules: Treat GGA/UAE–Belém and NAPs as the WG’s core negotiation streams unless CPs assign another track.
Keep child- and youth-responsive framing in GGA and NAP inputs; do not drop age- and gender-disaggregated asks without group agreement.
The SB64 WhatsApp and working docs are coordination spaces, not public announcement channels — do not share invite links outside YOUNGO without CP approval.
Coordinate interventions and public statements with the Contact Points before using the YOUNGO Adaptation name.

presentation: Register as a YOUNGO member if you are not already one.
Complete the Food & Agriculture WG onboarding form (Contact Points Bruna, Imran, Laureen).
Read the members handbook for structure, channels, and how to contribute.
Use youngoagrifood.com for Academy sessions, publications, and the youth project map.
rules: The onboarding form requires constituency membership before WG onboarding.
Academy sessions are free and open to anyone under 35; 75% attendance is required for a certificate.
Questions go to the WG inbox, not personal emails.

presentation: Child Rights WG is YOUNGO’s platform for safe child participation and for keeping children’s rights in climate policy — CRC General Comment 26, child-responsive NDCs/NAPs/GGA, and safeguarding.
The official 2026 Contact Point roster lists no named CPs for Child Rights. Write the working-group inbox; do not expect a public WhatsApp or Drive link on this page.
Work often overlaps ACE, Health, Human Rights, and Women & Gender. Follow child-safeguarding rules in every shared space.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct, Safeguarding, and Child Safeguarding policies. Zero tolerance for abuse or exploitation.
Do not share images, names, or contact details of children without informed consent and CP/safeguarding guidance.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership.
Prioritise child-friendly communication and the right of children to be heard in climate decisions.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag safeguarding concerns through YOUNGO Awareness channels, not only this WG.

presentation: Cities WG amplifies youth voices on urban climate action: adaptation and resilience, city-led mitigation, health in cities, and meaningful participation in local governance.
Contact Points Dylan Flayyih, Armaan Choudhary, and Sonia Ugwunna coordinate the group. Public writing with ICLEI CityTalk and COP30 on-ground work are recent examples of WG output.
There is no public join form on the current roster. Use the Linktree and Notion site, then email the WG inbox. Register as a YOUNGO member first.
rules: Treat youth urban engagement as power-sharing, not one-off consultations.
Coordinate with other constituencies (especially LGMA) without speaking for them.
Coordinate public statements with Contact Points before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Conflict of Interest is a YOUNGO thematic working group on integrity in climate spaces. The UNFCCC track it follows is Arrangements for Intergovernmental Meetings (AIM) under the SBI, plus conflict-of-interest and Accountability Framework asks.

2026 Contact Points: Gabriele Leggeri and Rondouba Mbaiadem Rochto. The 2026 WG/OT roster does not publish a join form, WhatsApp, or Drive for this group. Register as a YOUNGO member first, then reach CPs through the roster.

Public work is often cross-constituency. At SB64, YOUNGO joined ENGO, TUNGO, and the Women and Gender Constituency on an AIM intervention covering defender safety, observer space, visas, and conflicts of interest. YOUNGO has also co-signed civil-society submissions for a UNFCCC Accountability Framework.

Read the YOUNGO Conflict of Interest Policy before contributing. Individuals and NGOs must honestly address political, polluting, and financial conflicts. Disclosure of industry ties at COP is not the same as a conflict-of-interest policy.
rules: Declare political, polluting, and financial conflicts of interest under the YOUNGO Conflict of Interest Policy. Do not wait to be asked.
You may describe work you do in the group. You may not speak or act on behalf of YOUNGO or this WG unless selected through a formal process.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct, Safeguarding policies, and UNFCCC NGO participation guidelines in all spaces, including AIM rooms and press events.
Do not invent or circulate private WhatsApp, Drive, or join links that are not on the public roster. Ask CPs through the WG/OT contacts page.
Coordinate interventions, submissions, and public statements with CPs. AIM and COI asks are often joint with other rights-based constituencies — do not freelance YOUNGO positions.
Credit collective work. Treat observer lists, draft texts, and unpublished WG drafts as internal unless CPs say otherwise.

presentation: This Hub group covers Local, Regional, and Global Conferences of Youth (LCOY / RCOY / COY) as one coordination space. Those conferences feed National and Regional Youth Statements into the Global Youth Statement.
COY21 is 5–7 November 2026 in Antalya, Türkiye, ahead of COP31. climatecoy.com is the current COY / LCOY / RCOY / GYS site; history remains on the UNFCCC COY page.

2026 LCOY liaisons are Dr. Anirudh Janagam (India) and Jeremy Nathanael (Indonesia). RCOY 2026 liaison seats are blank on the WG/OT roster. Use the LCOY WG inbox listed in the directory for coordination.
rules: LCOYs and RCOYs are YOUNGO-endorsed, youth-led conferences — not UNFCCC events. Use YOUNGO endorsement language only when a conference is actually approved.
Do not promise badges, travel, or COY/COP attendance. Volunteer and delegate calls do not guarantee a seat.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all conference and WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without liaison approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole LCOY/RCOY/COY process unless mandated.

presentation: This Working Group coordinates thematic work inside YOUNGO — drafting, campaigns, and inputs to UNFCCC processes.
Contact Points (CPs) facilitate calls and channels. Members contribute in good faith and respect YOUNGO policies.
After you accept the rules, you unlock the WG module: WhatsApp (where available), CP contacts, and WG activities.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Energy WG works on a just energy transition — scaling renewables, phasing out fossil fuels, and energy access for young people and frontline communities.

Contact Points Dimple Asopa, Saikat Das, and Alex Lew facilitate advocacy, GYS inputs, and capacity-building. The group tracks mitigation and energy agenda items and uses open data such as Climate Watch and the Climate Action Tracker.

Join through the roster Jotform guide or the Linktree membership form. The WG website, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Beyond Energy Negotiations podcast carry public updates. Channel links follow after membership is confirmed.
rules: Ground claims in cited, verifiable sources when drafting submissions.
Centre a just transition and the needs of fossil-fuel-dependent and energy-poor communities.
Coordinate public statements with Contact Points before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Finance & Markets leads YOUNGO advocacy on climate and sustainable finance: NCQG follow-up, the Standing Committee on Finance, International Financial Architecture and Article 2.1c, UNFCCC funds, and Article 6 carbon markets.
Contact Points Marguerita Delgado and Timon Steger facilitate calls, channels, and submissions. Members research, draft, and join capacity-building such as the Climate Finance Academy.
Join via the roster Google Form or the Airtable form on Linktree, then use the shared Drive, WhatsApp, and call minutes. Confirm 2026 membership on the renewal form if you already joined earlier.
rules: Keep finance-sensitive drafts inside agreed channels.
Use inclusive language; centre climate justice and developing-country youth access to grant-based finance.
Coordinate public statements with Contact Points before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Women & Gender WG champions gender-responsive climate policy inside YOUNGO — GAP follow-up, CSW inputs, and intergenerational equity across UNFCCC tracks.
The official 2026 Contact Point roster lists no named CPs for this group. Use the public WhatsApp invite and the onboarding deck; confirm current facilitators on the WG/OT Notion roster.
Public entry points: WhatsApp, LinkedIn (women-and-gender-working-group), the 2026 policy roadmap, and the resource bank.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces, including gender-inclusive language on calls and chats.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without facilitator approval.
Centre women, girls, and gender-diverse people in all their diversity; do not treat gender as an add-on to other agenda items.
Coordinate public statements with WG facilitators before using the YOUNGO name.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest when relevant.

presentation: Health WG works at the climate–health nexus inside YOUNGO — NDC health and SRHR asks, climate-resilient health systems, and WHO–UNFCCC engagement.

2026 Contact Points are Aishat Oduye and Sıla Gürbüz (announced on Instagram @youngo.health, June 2026). CPs facilitate calls and channels; they do not speak for the whole constituency unless mandated.
Public updates live on LinkedIn (youngo-health-working-group) and Instagram (@youngo.health). Meeting and WhatsApp links are shared after membership, not as a public invite.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Ground health claims in cited sources (WHO, UNFCCC, peer-reviewed evidence) when drafting submissions.
Centre children, youth, and frontline communities in health–climate asks; coordinate public statements with CPs before using the YOUNGO name.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Human Rights WG works to keep human rights in climate negotiations and YOUNGO policy — SB/COP papers, the Global Youth Statement, and civic-space asks.
The group has three subgroups: Administration (events and coordination), Policy (papers and YOUNGO policy work), and Communications (social media and rights-related days).

2026 Contact Points are Doğukan and Abischag (official roster). Fill the membership form; WhatsApp and meeting links are sent after you review the onboarding slides — they are not posted as a public invite.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Do not put environmental human rights defenders or at-risk observers at further risk in public posts or chats.
Coordinate public statements with CPs before using the YOUNGO name.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: The Just Transition WG is YOUNGO’s group on just transition and green jobs. Members work through the Policy Team, the Capacity Building Team, the Fossil Fuel Phase-out Taskforce, and cross-constituency partnerships.

2026 Contact Points are Amany Darkaoui (Imane Darkaoui on the constituency roster) and Masagus Fathan. Policy facilitators are Luna, Rajia, and Doğukan. Capacity-building facilitators are Priyanka and Abhinav.
The self-paced introduction walks through the 2026 map: the UAE Just Transition Work Programme, the Just Transition Mechanism, response measures and the KCI, and how to join a sub-team.
rules: Keep just-transition asks rights-based: labour rights, social dialogue, social protection, and the needs of fossil-fuel-dependent and informal workers.
Distinguish the UNFCCC JTWP from regional instruments such as the EU Just Transition Mechanism.
Coordinate public statements with Contact Points before using the YOUNGO name.
Join at least one sub-team or taskforce. General Meetings are where the whole group hears sub-team updates and political moments.
Check the mailing list and WhatsApp often enough to reply or react, and leave threads you cannot follow.

presentation: The Loss & Damage Working Group is YOUNGO’s platform on UNFCCC loss-and-damage issues: the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), the Warsaw International Mechanism, and the Santiago Network.
2026 Contact Points are Jasmima Sabatina (also FRLD Active Observer Liaison) and Kartik PSW. Join via the public form; you must already be a YOUNGO member.
The join form states four operating principles: democratic processes, openness, youth-driven initiatives, and representation of YOUNGO rather than individual organisations.
rules: WG decisions are democratic; Contact Points coordinate and represent those decisions, not personal positions.
Membership is open to YOUNGO members; YOUNGO rules apply in all L&D spaces.
Keep positions youth-driven and independent of partner organisations when speaking as the WG.
Coordinate public statements, observer inputs, and FRLD/WIM/Santiago Network representation with the Contact Points.

presentation: Migration WG works on climate-related human mobility — migration, displacement, and the rights of young people on the move — inside YOUNGO.
Public updates run through X (@YOUNGOMIGRATION). Day-to-day coordination is on WhatsApp. No separate public join form or WG inbox is on file.
2026 Contact Points Ayomipo Ademilusi, Joseph Pasfield, and Rahma Kiriwe (announced on the WG X account, 4 April 2026).
rules: Centre the dignity, safety, and consent of migrants, displaced people, and host communities in all drafts and posts.
Do not share personal stories or identifiable case material without explicit consent.
Coordinate public statements and UNFCCC/IOM inputs with CPs before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.

presentation: The Mitigation Working Group follows UNFCCC mitigation tracks, including the Sharm el-Sheikh mitigation ambition and implementation work programme (MWP), which Parties set up to scale mitigation this decade in a way that complements the global stocktake.
2026 Contact Point is Gaëtan De Baene. The 2026 roster has no public join URL; ask the Contact Point via the constituency WG/OT roster after you are a YOUNGO member.
The MWP is scheduled through CMA 8 in 2026, with at least two global dialogues and investment-focused events each year. Outcomes are non-prescriptive and do not impose new targets.
rules: Ground mitigation claims in cited sources (UNFCCC documents, IPCC, CAT) when drafting inputs.
Do not treat MWP dialogues as a mandate to announce new YOUNGO emission targets; the work programme is facilitative and nationally determined.
Coordinate public statements and interventions with the Contact Point before using the YOUNGO Mitigation name.
There is no public join form in the 2026 roster — do not circulate unofficial signup links.

presentation: Register as a YOUNGO member if you are not already one.
Fill the Nature WG join form (forms.gle/7GxnEGetVKE3geSa7).
Follow LinkedIn, Instagram, and Linktree for task-force and meeting updates — no public 2026 call cadence is posted.
rules: The join form requires official YOUNGO membership.
The official 2026 WG/OT roster lists no current Nature Contact Points — do not treat 2025 form signatures as 2026 CPs.
The July 2026 task-force interest sheet window closed 20 July; watch LinkedIn for the first meeting of the term.

presentation: The NDCs Working Group supports young people to understand and follow NDCs, build youth capacity, improve engagement in revision and implementation, and represent youth voices in UNFCCC processes.

2026 Contact Points are Zipporah Njenga (Kenya) and Salsalina Larasati (Indonesia). The self-paced introduction is the group’s 2025/2026 onboarding deck: YOUNGO’s history and mission, what an NDC is, the four support teams, and the Global Stocktake.

Join at least one support team — Global Stocktake, Communications, Policy & Submissions, or Capacity Building — via the public form. You should already be a YOUNGO member. Meeting links stay with registered members.
rules: Join at least one of the four subgroups named on the join form.
When contributing to Global Youth Statement or NDC drafts, do not edit or delete others’ inputs and do not submit AI-generated text (as stated on the WG’s 2026 GYS call).
Do not circulate internal meeting links; Instagram notes that meeting details go to registered members.
Coordinate public statements and NDC Basics / Climate Week representation with the Contact Points.

presentation: Register as a YOUNGO member (constituency membership form).
Use the Ocean's Voice Linktree as the public entry — the community Google Form on that Linktree currently 404s.
Follow Instagram @youngo_oceansvoice and LinkedIn YOUNGO Ocean's Voice for 2026 updates.
rules: Constituency membership is the usual path into WG channels.
Prefer Linktree over the older Wix site for current join paths.
Do not use the 2024 Google Meet still listed on Linktree as a current call.

presentation: Peace & Security WG (Climate Peace and Security) focuses on climate-specific destabilisation that hits youth — food, water and energy access, displacement, and human security — and on climate action as peacebuilding.
2026 Contact Points are Doğukan Ejder and Yosr Khèdr (official roster). Join via the membership form; WhatsApp is collected on the form, not published as an open invite.
The LinkedIn page states three pillars: climate-related security threats, climate initiatives as peacebuilding, and sustainability in the defence and space sectors and supply chains.
rules: Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Treat conflict-affected and displaced communities with care; do not publish identifying details that could increase risk.
Ground security claims in cited sources; do not speculate about ongoing conflicts as YOUNGO.
Coordinate public statements with CPs before using the YOUNGO name.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: The Science Working Group is a YOUNGO space for children and youth to learn climate science, the science–policy interface, and science diplomacy, including engagement with the IPCC.
2026 Contact Points are Jude Earls and Debosmita Ghosh. Join via the public form (bit.ly/YOUNGO_SWG_2025); the form still carries a 2025 title but is the roster join URL.
The Hub’s Resources section is an open collection of climate work, research, learning, and funding. IPCC assessments are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
rules: When citing IPCC or other assessments, keep the distinction: they inform policy; they do not prescribe it.
Do not present personal research or unpublished results as WG or YOUNGO science without CP agreement.
Credit collective Hub and translation work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
The join form may still list a previous-term personal contact — use the 2026 Contact Points (Jude Earls, Debosmita Ghosh) via constituency channels, not personal Gmail from the form.

presentation: The Technology Mechanism Working Group follows UNFCCC technology development and transfer: the Technology Executive Committee (policy) and the Climate Technology Centre and Network (implementation), including equitable access for developing countries, LDCs, and SIDS.

Contact Points Asja Begić and Benita Clement facilitate YOUNGO observer engagement with TEC and CTCN processes. There is no public join URL on the current roster — ask the Contact Points after you register as a YOUNGO member.
Start with TT:CLEAR for official documents, TEC meeting papers, and Technology Mechanism mandates such as the Belém Technology Implementation Programme.
rules: Ground technology asks in TEC/CTCN mandates and cited official documents.
Centre equitable access, including for LDCs and SIDS, and avoid speaking as if all climate tech is equally available.
Coordinate public statements with Contact Points before using the YOUNGO name.
Follow the YOUNGO Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies in all WG spaces.
Do not share private channel links outside YOUNGO membership without CP approval.
Credit collective work; do not speak for the whole WG unless mandated.
Flag conflicts of interest to the CP when relevant.

presentation: Register as a YOUNGO member via the constituency membership form.
Open the official WG/OT roster for Contact Points — none are named for Water in 2026.
Until a Water CP or join form is published, follow constituency channels rather than a dedicated Water page.

slides.title: Welcome to Just Transition WG
body: YOUNGO Just Transition Working Group
Just transition, green jobs, and the road to COP31.

slides.title: Why Just Transition WG?
body: Countries act on climate change through policies, programmes, and investments. Those choices change work, communities, industries, and trade.
Just transition is the work of handling those consequences fairly. This working group is where youth in YOUNGO coordinate on that.

slides.title: Four places to contribute
body: The working group sits inside YOUNGO. Day-to-day work happens in teams, a taskforce, and cross-constituency partnerships.

points.label: Policy Team

The 2026 ambition is to invite people from the working group into that team, continue the Just Transition Academy, and collaborate with other working groups and organisations. What it asks of you is creativity, initiative, and a willingness to make the work usable for someone else.

slides.title: Three just-transition spaces
body: Response measures are the policies, programmes, and actions countries take to address climate change, and the socioeconomic impacts of those actions on workers, communities, industries, and trade. The group’s briefing splits the UNFCCC just-transition work into three spaces.

points.label: In a country
points.text: A coal phase-out changes local mining jobs.

points.label: Across borders
points.text: A carbon border measure such as CBAM changes exporters in other countries.

points.label: In a sector
points.text: A shift in agricultural subsidies changes farming livelihoods.

points.label: KCI — technical
points.text: The Katowice Committee of Experts, set up at COP24, studies what happens when climate policies land.

points.label: UAE JTWP — political
points.text: The UAE Just Transition Work Programme is where Parties negotiate and set norms.

points.label: Mechanism — implementation
points.text: The BAM space COP30 agreed to develop, being built toward COP31.

slides.title: What to keep watching at the KCI
body: The May 2026 briefing asks members to keep these items in view as the KCI works through its next workplan. Meetings are webcast. An in-person session needs a conference badge. Notes come back to the working group.

points.label: Co-chairs

points.label: Cross-border impacts
points.text: Measures such as CBAM, and their effects on developing countries, stay a live North–South question.

points.label: Local assessment tools
points.text: A toolbox for countries to assess impacts at home is a place to ask for youth-inclusive methods.

points.label: Case studies on decent work

slides.title: NDCs Working Group
body: Nationally Determined Contributions
By Salsalina Larasati and Zipporah Njenga.

slides.title: Our history
body: And the story that continues with your climate activism.

points.label: 1992 · Rio Earth Summit
points.text: Principle 21 of the Rio Declaration identified nine sectors, including children and youth.

points.label: 2005 · COP11 Montreal
points.text: Youth gathered in Montreal ahead of COP11 to be heard as the International Youth Climate Movement.

points.label: 2009 · COP15 Copenhagen
points.text: The UNFCCC secretariat and Parties officially recognized youth as an observer constituency of its own.

points.label: 2011 · Constituency confirmation
points.text: YOUNGO was formalized as the voice of children and youth in UNFCCC processes.

slides.title: Our mission
body: YOUNGO focuses on four areas.

points.label: Awareness and capacity
points.text: Awareness, knowledge, and capacity building.

points.label: Collaboration
points.text: Collaboration, cooperation, and networking.

points.label: Policy and advocacy
points.text: Policy, lobby, and advocacy.

points.label: Youth action
points.text: Youth action, locally and in the process.

slides.title: Our vision
body: We aim and envision:

points.label: A livable planet
points.text: A climate-positive and just society living in harmony with nature and the planet.

points.label: An empowered generation
points.text: Youth driving meaningful, impactful, and positive change locally, nationally, and internationally.

points.label: A seat at the table
points.text: A UN where youth sits at the decision-making tables and is taken seriously.

slides.title: What this group is for
body: The NDCs Working Group is one of YOUNGO’s active groups. It has four jobs.

points.label: Understand and follow
points.text: Support young people to understand, monitor, and follow NDCs and related topics.

points.label: Build momentum
points.text: Build youth momentum for NDCs by strengthening the capacity of young people.

points.label: Engage in the process
points.text: Improve youth engagement in NDC revision and implementation.

points.label: Represent youth
points.text: Represent youth voices on NDCs and related topics in UNFCCC processes.

slides.title: Why should youth engage in NDCs?
body: Young people stand to bear the brunt of future impacts from climate crises. Youth have the passion, knowledge, energy, and creativity to translate climate action plans such as NDCs into action, by mobilizing communities on the ground and holding leaders accountable at all levels.
Active participation of youth is a must for the success of NDCs.

slides.title: Four support teams
body: 2026 Contact Points are Zipporah Njenga (Kenya) and Salsalina Larasati (Indonesia). Join at least one team on the public form. You should already be a YOUNGO member.

points.label: Global Stocktake
points.text: GST processes, submissions, and how stocktake outcomes connect to NDCs. The join form calls this subgroup Global Stocktake.

points.label: Communications
points.text: How the group explains its work, including the public Instagram and LinkedIn channels.

points.label: Policies & Submissions
points.text: Youth inputs on NDC revision, implementation, and UNFCCC processes. The join form calls this Policy & Submissions.

points.label: Capacity building
points.text: Help young people learn NDCs, including their own country’s NDC, and how to engage.

slides.title: What an NDC is
body: Climate actions that Parties to the Paris Agreement plan to undertake to address climate change.

points.label: Nationally determined
points.text: A Party’s contribution reflects its national circumstances and priorities.

points.label: Heart of the Paris Agreement
points.text: The NDC is the heart of the Paris Agreement, the first binding agreement for climate action.

points.label: Every five years
points.text: Each Party is required to establish an NDC and update it every five years.

slides.title: What the plan has to do

points.label: Targets
points.text: Countries set targets for mitigating the greenhouse gas emissions that cause climate change, and for adapting to climate impacts.

points.label: How to get there
points.text: The plans define how to reach the targets, and systems to monitor and verify progress so it stays on track.

points.label: Finance
points.text: Because climate finance is key to implementing the plans, NDCs ideally also detail a financing strategy.

points.label: Government lead
points.text: An NDC is a government obligation under the Paris Agreement. One or more national ministries generally lead its development.

points.label: Wider than government
points.text: For NDCs to work, businesses, civil society, academia, and ordinary citizens need to understand and use them.

points.label: A role for constituencies
points.text: Each has a role, which is why many governments invite constituencies to take part in defining NDC priorities.

slides.title: Why NDCs matter
body: The actions in all NDCs are the collective global effort. Together they determine whether the world achieves the long-term temperature goal of the Paris Agreement.

slides.title: How progress is tracked
body: With the Paris Agreement, countries established an enhanced transparency framework (ETF). Information gathered through the ETF feeds the Global Stocktake, which assesses collective progress toward the long-term climate goals.
That assessment leads to recommendations for countries to set more ambitious plans in the next round.

slides.title: Youth engagement in NDCs
body: Good practices the onboarding deck records for this group.

points.label: Learn the NDC
points.text: Empower young people to learn about NDCs, their country’s NDC, and how to engage in formulation and implementation, including through infographics and webinars.

points.label: Across countries
points.text: Young people from more than 70 countries have shared good practices and challenges of implementing NDCs at home.

points.label: Youth-inclusive checklist
points.text: The group worked with UNDP and other youth partners on a youth-inclusive NDC checklist to strengthen youth involvement in implementation.

points.label: Country offices
points.text: The group explores collaboration that connects young people with local UNDP country offices for on-the-ground NDC and youth-engagement work.

slides.title: What the Global Stocktake is
body: The Global Stocktake (GST) takes stock of how the Paris Agreement is being implemented.

points.label: Article 14
points.text: It assesses the world’s collective progress toward the purpose of the Agreement and its long-term goals.

points.label: The first cycle
points.text: The first GST ran from 2021 to 2023. The process repeats every five years.

slides.title: Thematic areas of the GST
body: The GST assesses global collective progress on three thematic areas. Equity is taken into account, and the assessment uses the best available science in a cross-cutting way.

points.label: Mitigation
points.text: Collective progress on cutting greenhouse gas emissions.

points.label: Adaptation
points.text: Collective progress on adapting to climate impacts.

points.label: Means of implementation
points.text: Means of implementation and support, including finance, technology, and capacity-building.

slides.title: Why the GST matters for NDCs
body: GST outcomes inform countries as they update and enhance their climate action plans, and as they enhance international cooperation for climate action.
Those outputs are key political messages and recommendations, best practices, new opportunities, and lessons learned across the thematic areas.

slides.title: Youth engagement in the GST
body: Good practices the onboarding deck records for the stocktake.

points.label: Explain the link
points.text: Understand why the GST matters and how it links to NDCs, then build on that message with capacity-building sessions through the year.

points.label: Follow the process
points.text: Follow GST discussions at the Subsidiary Bodies, at COP, and in between sessions.

points.label: Three submissions
points.text: The group has submitted three times on the GST, with other YOUNGO working groups and broader youth groups.

points.label: Cross-constituency taskforce
points.text: A cross-constituency taskforce coordinates so demands line up with one another.

slides.kicker: How to be an active member
slides.title: Join a team, then the channels
body: Use the public join form and pick at least one support team. The onboarding deck also points to the WhatsApp community and the public social channels. Meeting links stay with registered members.

points.label: One support team
points.text: Global Stocktake, Communications, Policies & Submissions, or Capacity building.

points.label: Contact Points
points.text: Zipporah Njenga and Salsalina Larasati facilitate the group. Coordinate public statements and NDC Basics or Climate Week representation with them.

slides.title: Now let us hear from you
body: The deck closes by asking for your expectations and aspirations.
When you unlock the workspace, tell the Contact Points which support team you are joining and what you want to work on.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: Who is responsible for your data
paragraphs: YOUNGO — the Children and Youth Constituency of the UNFCCC — is responsible for the personal data collected through the YOUNGO Hub. The platform is operated day to day by the YOUNGO Hub Team, which is accountable to YOUNGO Council.
If you want to reach a person about anything in this notice, email membership@youngoclimate.org. You do not need to give a reason.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: Why we ask for your consent separately
paragraphs: Accepting the Membership Policy tells you what membership in YOUNGO means. It is not the same thing as agreeing to let this platform hold your personal data.

So we ask for those separately. You read this notice, then you give a distinct consent, and we record which version of this notice you consented to and when. If this notice changes in substance, we ask you again rather than assuming your old answer still applies.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: If you are under 18
paragraphs: If your date of birth shows you are under 18, the registration form will not let you finish without a guardian’s name, a guardian’s email, and a confirmation that your guardian has given permission. This follows the Membership Policy §1 and the YOUNGO Child Safeguarding Policy.

Guardian details are visible only to YOUNGO Hub admins and the Membership Team. They are not shown to other members, not shown to working group contact points, and never returned by search on the platform.
A guardian can withdraw permission at any time by emailing membership@youngoclimate.org, and the account will be closed and the data deleted.

bullets.label: Other members
items: Your name, and the working groups you have joined
Nothing else — not your date of birth, phone number, background information, guardian details, or motivation

bullets.label: Working group contact points
items: The name and email of members who join their own working group, so they can coordinate the work

bullets.label: YOUNGO Hub admins and the Membership Team
items: The full member record, in order to verify membership and administer the constituency
If an application is rejected, an identity document and statement you send with an appeal — used only to review that appeal
Never your password — it is stored only as a cryptographic hash and cannot be read or recovered by anyone

bullets.label: Nobody outside YOUNGO
items: Your data is not sold, rented, or shared with third parties for their own purposes
It is not used for advertising, and there is no advertising or third-party tracking on this platform
It is shared with the UNFCCC secretariat only where you have asked YOUNGO to act for you — for example a badge or submission request — and only what that request needs

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: What the Hub’s search and intelligence features can never reach
paragraphs: The Hub has a search feature that answers questions from YOUNGO’s documented record. It is walled off from personal data by design, not by convention.

Account records, passwords, sessions, guardian details, background and minority information, and personal email and phone fields are excluded from what it can retrieve — for every user, including administrators. Queries against it are logged so that the exclusion can be audited rather than taken on trust.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: How long your data is kept
paragraphs: While your membership is active, your account stays open and your record is kept up to date.
When membership ends, the adopted Membership Policy already sets the timelines the Hub follows:

bullets.label: On the timelines in the Membership Policy
items: Resignation — you email the Membership Team, and you are removed from all YOUNGO services within one month (§2.1)
Expiration — individual membership expires at 35; expired members are removed from YOUNGO services at least monthly (§2.2)
Termination — where membership is terminated under the Code of Conduct, removal is immediate (§2.3)

bullets.label: What the Hub does on top of that
items: Your Hub account is closed and your personal record deleted when you are removed from YOUNGO services
Guardian permission records are deleted when the account is closed, or when you turn 18 and they are no longer needed
Dormant accounts that never completed the membership course are deleted after 24 months without a sign-in
The governance audit log keeps a record that an action happened and who took it, because accountability requires it — but not the personal details of the member concerned

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: What you can ask for
paragraphs: These are yours to exercise at any time, and using them is never held against you.

bullets.label: You can ask to
items: See a copy of the data the Hub holds about you
Correct anything that is wrong — the Membership Policy §1.3 already provides for this by email
Delete your account and your data
Withdraw this consent, which closes your Hub account; withdrawing does not by itself end your YOUNGO membership, which is a separate process with the Membership Team
Object to a particular use of your data, or ask for an explanation of it
Raise a concern with YOUNGO Council if you are not satisfied with how the Hub Team answered you

paragraphsAfter: Email membership@youngoclimate.org for any of these. The Hub Team aims to answer within 30 days, and will tell you if it needs longer.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: How your data is protected

bullets.label: In place today
items: Passwords are stored only as cryptographic hashes — administrators cannot see or recover them
Sign-in sessions are stored hashed, in cookies that scripts on the page cannot read
Password reset links are single-use, expire after one hour, and are stored hashed
Access is role-based: contact points, organisation seats, and administrators each see only what their role requires
Role and permission changes are written to a governance audit log
The connection to the platform is encrypted in transit

paragraphsAfter: No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal data, the Hub Team will notify affected members and report to YOUNGO Council without undue delay.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: Where your data is held
paragraphs: The platform and its database are hosted on Railway, a cloud infrastructure provider, which processes the data on YOUNGO’s behalf and under its instructions. Railway does not use YOUNGO member data for its own purposes.
Because the constituency is global, data may be processed outside your own country. Access remains restricted to the roles described above wherever it is hosted.

PRIVACY_SECTIONS.heading: If this notice changes
paragraphs: Every version of this notice carries a version identifier, and the version you consented to is recorded against your account.

If what is collected, why, who can see it, how long it is kept, or who processes it changes, the version is bumped and you are asked to review and consent again. You will not be quietly moved onto new terms.
Any change that affects what personal data is collected goes back to YOUNGO Council before it takes effect.

FAQ.a: Yes. You passed the membership course and your Hub account is verified. You can return here at any time to review the course or open the library.

FAQ.q: What should I do first as a verified member?
FAQ.a: Check Home for current meetings and deadlines, then open Calendar and Working groups. Each group has a short introduction and its own participation rules.

FAQ.q: Do I still need the Membership Team onboarding call?
FAQ.a: Yes, if the Membership Team asks you to attend. The Hub course verifies your account, but it does not replace YOUNGO membership processes or the July and December Constituency Work onboarding cycles.

FAQ.q: How do Working Groups work from here?
FAQ.a: The interests selected during registration are preferences, not memberships. Open a group, enter its workspace, read the introduction, and accept the rules. The Hub will then show that group’s channel links and Contact Point details.

FAQ.q: Where do I find submissions, Council decisions, and COYs?
FAQ.a: Use Submissions, Council, and COY tracker in the main navigation. Home also shows approaching deadlines.

FAQ.q: Where is my accredited NGO workspace?
FAQ.a: If you registered an organisation or accepted a seat invitation, open NGO platform in the sidebar. It contains deadlines, endorsement and submission requests, and team seats. Members without an organisation seat do not see it.

FAQ.q: Can I speak on behalf of YOUNGO?
FAQ.a: Not unless you have been selected through the relevant YOUNGO process. A verified Hub account does not make someone a spokesperson for YOUNGO or a working group.

FAQ.q: How does the Hub use my personal data?
FAQ.a: The Privacy Notice explains what the registration form collects, why it is needed, who can see it, and how long it is kept. Your account records the notice version you accepted. Email membership@youngoclimate.org to request a copy, correction, or deletion.

FAQ.q: How do I reset my password or get help?
FAQ.a: Use Forgot password from the sign-in form, or ask an admin for a reset link. Send membership questions to membership@youngoclimate.org or youngomembership@gmail.com. Report Hub problems to your platform admin.

hero.eyebrow: The official children and youth constituency of the UNFCCC
hero.title: Your place in global climate action.
hero.lead: YOUNGO brings together young people, youth-led organisations, groups, and delegations working on climate change. Learn the UN climate process, contribute to policy, and meet people taking action around the world.
hero.reassurance: Open to children and youth up to 35. No membership fee.

mission.title: Four ways we work
mission.lead: There is no single way to take part. Start with the work that feels most useful to you.

items.title: Learn together
items.body: We help children and young people understand the UN climate process and build the skills to take part in it — from first-time followers to trained negotiators.

items.title: Connect across borders
items.body: We connect youth-led organisations, groups, delegations, and individuals across every region so local action adds up to a global movement.

items.title: Shape climate policy
items.body: We draft, coordinate, and deliver youth policy positions into the UNFCCC process, so the perspectives of young and future generations are heard where decisions are made.

items.title: Take action
items.body: We turn participation into agency: members run campaigns, actions, and initiatives inside and around the negotiations.

organisation.title: How YOUNGO is organised
organisation.lead: YOUNGO was designed by young people, for young people — with as little hierarchy as possible. Every member is invited to take the initiative: start a submission, an action, or a new working group.
organisation.note: Two Global Focal Points — one from the Global South, one from the Global North — are the constituency’s face to the UNFCCC Secretariat, COP hosts, and the other constituencies. A Global Coordination Team keeps an overview, working groups run independently, and the whole constituency meets on a monthly call.

stats.label: No hierarchies. Roles facilitate; they do not decide over others.
All decisions are taken by consensus via established decision-making guidelines.
Every engaging entity — irrespective of an NGO’s scale — has an equal voice.
The oldest and largest volunteer-run children and youth constituency to a UN convention.

takePart.title: What you can take part in

items.title: Submissions
items.body: Coordinated policy inputs to UNFCCC bodies, sessions, and workshops.

items.title: Global Youth Statement
items.body: Inputs from young people worldwide, synthesised into the statement presented at each COP.

items.title: Conferences of Youth
items.body: The annual COY and its local and regional editions (LCOY, RCOY) gather youth ahead of COP.

items.title: Working groups
items.body: Thematic groups — from Adaptation and Finance to Gender and Human Rights — do the day-to-day policy work.

items.title: Science resources
items.body: Reviewed research, learning, career, and funding resources for climate action.

items.title: Presence at negotiations
items.body: Members follow COP, SB, and intersessional agenda items and coordinate daily as one constituency.

principles.title: Values & principles
principles.lead: Our principles guide how members work together. YOUNGO condemns all types of harassment; an internal Awareness Team and a Code of Conduct — including an Anti-Harassment Policy — keep the space safe and open.

items.title: The youth climate movement
items.body: Young people take part in UNFCCC sessions through observer organisations under the self-organised umbrella of the International Youth Climate Movement (IYCM).

items.title: Provisional constituency status
items.body: Ahead of COP15 in Copenhagen, the UNFCCC Secretariat and member states grant youth provisional observer constituency status — formalised as YOUNGO.

items.title: Official recognition
items.body: The constituency status becomes official. YOUNGO is confirmed as the formal voice of children and youth in UNFCCC processes.

items.title: Oldest and largest
items.body: More than a decade later, YOUNGO remains volunteer-run and youth-led — the oldest and largest children and youth constituency to a UN convention or entity.

coy.title: The Conference of Youth
coy.lead: The Conference of Youth (COY) is YOUNGO’s most important annual event and is rooted in a long history. It serves as a gathering of members of the constituency and youth interested in the work of YOUNGO — usually in the same city as the COP, in the days preceding it. Local and regional editions feed into it, and its outputs culminate in the Global Youth Statement presented at the COP.

formats.title: COY — the global Conference of Youth
formats.body: The most important annual event of YOUNGO. It is usually organised in the same city as the COP and takes place in the days preceding it, gathering members of the constituency and youth interested in YOUNGO’s work. Its outputs feed formally into YOUNGO’s work at the COP.

formats.title: RCOY — Regional COY
formats.body: Regional Conferences of Youth bring LCOY inputs together by UN region, draft a Regional Youth Statement (RYS), and feed that into the Global Youth Statement.

formats.title: LCOY — Local COY
formats.body: National and sub-national gatherings hosted by children and young people. Each LCOY builds a National Youth Statement (NYS) for home advocacy and for the global statement.

formats.title: vCOY — virtual COY
formats.body: The virtual Conference of Youth keeps the process open year-round, in line with YOUNGO’s mandate and policy processes aimed towards the UN and especially the UNFCCC.

cta.title: Be part of the next COY
cta.body: Every COY is run by volunteer teams — coordinators, delegates, and organisers from around the world. Join the Hub to find your regional team and take part.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Everything newcomers usually want to know about YOUNGO — how it works, who can join, and how it fits into the UN climate process.

items.a: All children and youth up to the age of 35 can join YOUNGO — individually or through a youth-led organisation, group, delegation, or network. Membership is free. It is impossible to represent “all” youth, so YOUNGO strives to listen to and engage every young person who wants to take part.

YOUNGO has a structure with as little hierarchy as possible. Every member is invited to take the initiative and start a submission, action, or working group. The thematic working groups work quite independently, and the Global Coordination Team keeps an overview of engagement across the constituency. The two Global Focal Points — one from the Global South and one from the Global North — are responsible for communication with official entities, especially the UNFCCC Secretariat and COP hosts, and with the other constituencies. Once a month, members meet in a constituency call.

Flat, by design. None of YOUNGO’s roles and institutions have designated or de facto decision-making power; they function as facilitating and supporting elements for the wider constituency. All decisions are taken by consensus via established decision-making guidelines, and all engaging entities — different NGOs, irrespective of their scale — have an equal voice.

YOUNGO is an open, cost-free, and accessible space that aims to build a global community of youth working to solve the climate crisis. Inclusivity is at the heart of the constituency and reflected in its principles: a horizontal, decentralised, and non-hierarchical work ethic that welcomes constructive, critical, and diverse views. YOUNGO works to improve language diversity and accessibility for youth with special needs, refugees, and youth from marginalised communities. All members are expected to respect cultural differences and support each other. YOUNGO condemns all types of harassment and maintains an internal Awareness Team and a Code of Conduct, including an Anti-Harassment Policy.

items.q: Which language is used within YOUNGO?
items.a: The working language of the constituency is English. Members are continuously working to lower language barriers, including translations of key documents where capacity allows.

items.q: Does YOUNGO membership let me attend COP?
items.a: No. YOUNGO membership does not grant UNFCCC badges or a place in your country’s delegation. For a national delegation, contact the ministry in your country responsible for COP delegations. YOUNGO members can, however, follow the negotiations, join working groups, and contribute to constituency work year-round — and some members attend sessions through YOUNGO observer organisations.

items.q: What is the UNFCCC, and what is the COP?
items.a: The UNFCCC is the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change — the treaty framework under which countries negotiate the global response to climate change. The COP (Conference of the Parties) is its annual decision-making meeting. YOUNGO members observe and report on these negotiations and the implications of their outcomes.

The constituency is guided by its principles and its Code of Conduct. YOUNGO is one of the nine civil society constituencies officially recognised by the UNFCCC, and its internal structure was designed entirely by young people.

items.q: Where do I manage my membership?
items.a: Membership is managed through the YOUNGO Hub — the constituency’s member platform. Register, pass the short membership course, and the Hub opens: the constituency calendar, working groups, submissions, the Youth Statement process, opportunities, and the tools attached to your responsibilities.
